elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: "HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates..." — express defence duty running to Company and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "...the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)..."

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (1): "an allegation that the Site or any services or deliverables provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the Site/services/deliverables of this agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (3): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Content caused by HDI".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (4): "HDI's gross negligence or wilful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "The Company shall defend and indemnify HDI against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law." — confined to the two permitted triggers.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Limb (1) of the inserted HDI indemnity covers third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element ('may exclude'); no such exclusion is required, and none is inconsistent with the inserted text.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; absence of a combinations carve-out is more favourable to Customer and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications carve-out is needed for the fallback to be satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation for HDI.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual fees super-cap is included; the drafter expressly declined to add one (and only offered it in the comment).

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate of the first fallback element; satisfied by limb (1).

reasons: All ten preferred elements are met in the operative inserted paragraph: HDI defends/indemnifies Company and affiliates against third-party claims on all four required limbs (IP infringement of the Site/services/deliverables, breach of applicable law, HDI-caused unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company data/Content, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct), with notice, control of defence and settlement, and reasonable cooperation, and the Company indemnity is confined to Company-provided Content and Company's breach of applicable law.

The fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees, no 3× annual fees super-cap), but the redline is position-complete because the preferred level is fully met; the fallback is only offered in the comment, which is acceptable since it is not the relied-upon level.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a single concise indemnity paragraph placed after the warranties section as the redline guidance directs; no existing language (including Section 9(a)-(b) and the Globix acknowledgement) is deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or boilerplate is added. Declining to add the super-cap avoids importing a Vendor-favourable liability limit into an agreement with no cap.

Intent is preserved: the clause uses defined terms already in the Agreement (HDI, Company, Site, Content), introduces no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, does not renumber Sections 9 or 10, and does not contradict any retained provision (the Section 7.2 mutual advertising covenant remains intact and is not duplicated).

Minor drafting notes for the record (not defects): the paragraph is unnumbered and could be styled as Section 9(c) or a new Section 10 with consequential renumbering; and the indemnity procedure conditions are drafted mutually, which is consistent with the two-way indemnity structure.
